title: WBS Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **The income limit is not your salary.** The Wohnungsamt starts with gross income, takes off the **1,230 euro** employee allowance for each earner, then up to **three separate ten percent deductions** for tax, health cover and pension. A normal payslip loses **thirty percent** before anything is compared.

**Berlin issues five certificates, not one.** The federal line is **12,000 euro** for a single household. Berlin raises it by law, so a single person also has a **WBS 140 at 16,800**, a **160 at 19,200**, a **180 at 21,600** and a narrow **220 at 26,400**.

**Read those as gross and they change shape.** A single employee clears a **WBS 180 on about 32,090 euro** a year, roughly **2,670 euro a month before tax**. Two adults on payslips clear the same band on about **48,750 euro**, and two adults with two children on about **72,400 euro**.

**A flatshare cannot apply together.** Separate certificates cannot be pooled and a joint application needs people who are related or who sign a Partnerschaftserklaerung. One room per person is the size rule, with a single person allowed up to **50 square metres**.

**Qualifying easily is not the same as qualifying usefully.** Almost every social flat in Berlin asks for a **WBS 100 or 140**. The 160, 180 and 220 bands cover the newer subsidised blocks and buying a share in a housing cooperative.

**It is free, it lasts a year, and it works citywide.** Apply at the Buergeramt or Wohnungsamt where you are registered, or online. The slow part is the **Einkommensbescheinigung**, which your employer has to sign, so ask for that first.
